title: Once-for-All subnetwork Mirror correction
hypothesis: A small width-addressed Mirror gate on shared supernet channels can recover three width-specific linear target functions with lower actual payload bytes than independent subnetworks and outperform byte-matched ordinary coefficient views.
mirror_coordinate: per-width diagonal gain vector on selected nested-prefix channels

development.selection_metric: mean test nMSE, actual serialized bytes, matrix MAC proxy

fresh.reason: Mirror and direct coefficient control are algebraically identical parameterizations; the registered direct-control gate adjudicates specificity.

storage.authority: actual deterministic NPZ payload bytes including metadata

success_gate: All widths mean nMSE <= 1e-3, Mirror uses >=10% fewer bytes than independent specialization, and >=10% fewer bytes than direct coefficient at matched quality.
failure_gate: Direct coefficient control matches Mirror within 1% bytes and quality, or target quality threshold fails.
boundaries: no hardware latency or task capacity claim
